ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, the perimeter of $\triangle ABC$ is 19. Points $D$ and $E$ are on side $BC$. The bisector of $\angle ABC$ is perpendicular to $AE$ at point $N$. The bisector of $\angle ACB$ is perpendicular to $AD$ at point $M$. If $BC = 7$, what is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the angle bisector of $\angle ABC$ is perpendicular to $AE$, with the foot of the perpendicular being point $N$, \\
it follows that $\angle ABN=\angle EBN$, and $\angle BNA=\angle BNE=90^\circ$, \\
In $\triangle BNA$ and $\triangle BNE$, \\
since $\left\{\begin{array}{l}\angle ABN=\angle EBN \\ BN=BN \\ \angle BNA=\angle BNE\end{array}\right.$, \\
it implies $\triangle BNA\cong \triangle BNE\left(ASA\right)$, \\
thus $BA=BE$, \\
Similarly, it can be proved that $\triangle CAM\cong \triangle CDM\left(ASA\right)$, \\
hence, $AC=DC$.\\
Given that the perimeter of $\triangle ABC$ is 19, \\
it follows that $AB+AC+BC=19$, \\
Since $BA=BE$ and $AC=DC$, \\
it follows that $BE+DC+BC=19$, \\
thus $BD+DE+DE+EC+BC=19$, \\
Given $BC=7$, \\
it follows that $BD+DE+DE+EC=19-BC=12$, \\
thus $BD+DE+EC+DE=BC+DE=12$, \\
which means $DE=12-BC=12-7=\boxed{5}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and BC is the horizontal base. Points D and E are on BC, in the order B-D-E-C. In the figure, the angle bisector drawn from B intersects segment AE at N, and the problem statement indicates that it is perpendicular to AE; the angle bisector drawn from C intersects segment AD at M, and the problem statement indicates that it is perpendicular to AD. Reasoning: Because BN is the angle bisector of ∠ABC, ∠ABN = ∠NBE; also because BN ⟂ AE, and A, N, E are collinear, ∠BNA = ∠BNE = 90°; plus BN is a common side, therefore △BNA ≅ △BNE, obtaining AB = BE. Similarly, because CM is the angle bisector of ∠ACB, and CM ⟂ AD, A, M, D are collinear, therefore △CMA ≅ △CMD, obtaining AC = CD. The perimeter of triangle ABC is 19, therefore AB + AC + BC = 19. Substituting AB = BE and AC = CD gives BE + CD + BC = 19. From the base order B-D-E-C, there are BE = BD + DE, CD = CE + DE, so BE + CD = BD + CE + 2DE. And BC = BD + DE + CE, therefore BE + CD = BC + DE. Thus 19 = BC + DE + BC = 2BC + DE. It is known that BC = 7, so DE = 19 - 2×7 = 5.
